title: PHP session writes and serializer mismatches can deserialize attacker-controlled objects
summary: Interrupted file-session writes can retain old serialized data. Separately, upload-progress sessions written and read with different serializers can turn attacker-controlled bytes into objects and trigger application gadget chains.

severity.rationale: Both paths can lead to remote code execution with a suitable application gadget chain. Session-content influence and interruption or shared-store serializer mismatch are required.

exposure: The interrupted-write flaw affects the default files handler. Serializer mismatch requires upload progress and shared session access with different serializers; separate FPM pools do not ensure separate stores.

params.instructions: Check PHP session extension version, affected release line and the documented exposure conditions.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 on the corresponding line.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed release meets the corresponding fixed version and verify the affected workflow with harmless test inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
